anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

bible_refs.note: Loose the sandal from your feet; the place is holy.
Loose the sandal; holy ground — possible parallel.

pass_a_gloss: He also says those chewing the pascha to have the shoes on the feet, which might seem to some a contradiction to the things used toward Moses. For since Moses was treading upon holy earth, he is commanded to loose the shoe from his feet. How then, the pascha also being holy, are those chewing this commanded to have their shoes bound on?
pass_b_english: He also says that those who chew the Passover are to have the shoes on their feet — which might seem to some a contradiction of what was used toward Moses. For since Moses was treading on holy ground, he is commanded to loose the shoe from his feet. How then, when the Passover too is holy, are those who chew it commanded to have their shoes bound on (Exodus 12:11) (Exodus 3:5) (Acts 7:33) (Joshua 5:15)?
source_text: Λέγει καὶ τὰ ὑποδήματα ἐν τοῖς ποσὶν [ἔ]χειν τοὺς τρώγοντας τὸ π[ά]σχα, ὅπερ ἐναντίωμα τ[ο]ῖς χρησθεῖσιν πρὸς Μωϋσῆ[ν] δόξειέ τισιν εἶναι· ἐπεὶ γὰρ Μ[ω]ϋσῆς ἐφ’ ἁγίαν ἐπάτει γ[ῆν], κελεύεται λῦσα<ι> τὸ ὑπό[δημ]α ἐκ τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ.
